verdict.rationale: Asana's own docs name first-party automation features: rule actions, AI Studio 'no-code automations,' and AI Teammates and agents that work inside workflows under governed permissions. Rules firing automatically is shown only indirectly, through a third-party integration listing (PagerDuty). The evidence is mostly marketing taglines and never describes how these automations are triggered, scheduled, or left to run unattended in the background. missing for 10: documentation of rule triggers/conditions and background execution, recurring or scheduled runs, documented autonomous AI Teammate actions without human prompting, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Automate tedious work in powerful, bespoke ways with our platform features like rule actions, webhooks, and our API.
Pre-built AI agents that work alongside your team inside real workflows
custom AI Teammates built to handle the complex, coordination-heavy work that slows your team down
Automatically create PagerDuty incidents with context from Asana tasks using Rules.
